{"path":"SOLUTION.md","content":"# Solution

Two bugs in `lrucache/cache.py`, both about LRU bookkeeping:

1. **`get` did not refresh recency.** A cache hit returned the value but never
   called `move_to_end`, so reads did not count as "use" and a recently-read
   entry could be evicted as least-recently-used. Fixed by calling
   `self._data.move_to_end(key)` on a successful (non-expired) hit.

2. **`put` evicted before checking for an existing key.** Updating a key that
   was already cached still popped the LRU entry first, shrinking the cache by
   one and evicting an innocent entry. Fixed by only evicting when the key is
   new and the cache is at capacity (`if key not in self._data and ...`).
"}

content:
Done. `python3 -m pytest -q` passes all 6 tests.

Two bugs in `lrucache/cache.py`:

- `get` never refreshed recency — a hit returned the value without `move_to_end`, so reads didn't count as use (`lrucache/cache.py:30`).
- `put` evicted unconditionally when at capacity, even when updating an existing key, shrinking the cache and evicting an unrelated entry (`lrucache/cache.py:33`).

Root causes are written up in `SOLUTION.md`.
